response: The Child Health Computing System (CHCS) does not adequately identify children with cerebral palsy. According to the available data, unless improvements are made in case ascertainment, case validation, and recording activities, the CHCS will not be able to provide the same quality of information for needs assessment and surveillance of very low birthweight infants in relation to cerebral palsy as is provided by a specialist case register. This suggests that the current system has limitations and may not accurately identify all cases of cerebral palsy, highlighting the need for enhancements to ensure reliable data collection and analysis.
